title: Chapter 64
content:
The heavy stench of alcohol rolling off Kang Il-hyun hit Jakyeong like a wall.

Writing it off as drunken belligerence was generous—this had crossed into sheer, unadulterated madness. There was a limit to human patience. After tormenting him in bed half the night, the bastard had drowned his phone in the pool that evening, and now he was kicking down locked doors with a fire axe, threatening to chop off his cock.

Tolerating another second of this made him a certified idiot.

Jakyeong lunged. He threw a lightning right cross, which Il-hyun slipped by a hair's breadth. He fired an immediate left hook, but Il-hyun caught his wrist, wrenching the joint into a tight armlock. Jakyeong snapped his arm free and drove a vicious shin kick straight into Il-hyun’s calf.

The heavy blow made Il-hyun stumble. Wheeling around, the man merely grinned.

"Touched a nerve, did I?"

Il-hyun stubbed his lit cigarette directly into the drywall, casually crooking two fingers. Bring it.

Dropping into a low combat stance, Jakyeong vaulted forward, driving an explosive flying knee upward. Il-hyun blocked the impact with crossed forearms, giving ground, only for Jakyeong to pivot into a blistering spinning heel kick.

The concussive strike rocked Il-hyun off-balance. Seizing the opening, Jakyeong tackled him mid-stride.

Both men went crashing onto the king-sized mattress in a violent tangle of limbs. Reaching above his head, Jakyeong ripped the embedded hatchet from the headboard, driving the steel blade straight down at Il-hyun's face.

Il-hyun rolled his head aside just in time—the sharp edge cleaving into the down pillow where his skull had rested a split second prior.

Realizing the kid was playing for keeps, Il-hyun clamped an iron grip around Jakyeong's forearms, heaving him off. Jakyeong rolled over the edge, scrambled to his feet, and hurled the heavy hatchet like a throwing axe.

Il-hyun ducked; the steel embedded deep into the opposite drywall with a dull thunk.

Looking back at the vibrating handle, Il-hyun’s brow furrowed. "Were you genuinely trying to take my head off? I'm your employer."

Panting in ragged heaves, Jakyeong flashed a stiff middle finger, his jaw grinding with pure venom. "Fuck off, you raving lunatic! The contract is void. I'm packing my bags and leaving this house at dawn."

"Then why did you have to go and ruin my mood by taking calls from your former flame?"

Jakyeong shouted in sheer disbelief. "You said out of your own mouth you didn't hold grudges!"

Il-hyun tilted his chin up with shameless arrogance. "I didn't. But I developed one tonight."

His jaw set into a petulant, displeased scowl.

"Was Veronica's body really that voluptuous? My cock is pretty damn voluptuous too—care for another look?"

The second Il-hyun reached for his waistband, Jakyeong surged forward without a word. Il-hyun threw up a tight, disciplined guard, but a vicious straight right broke through the defense, connecting with a brutal, concussive crack across his jaw.

Il-hyun’s head snapped sideways, his expression darkening into a ferocious, dangerous scowl.

As Jakyeong followed up with a barrage of hooks, Il-hyun parried the combinations, countering with a heavy straight right of his own.

Thud.

The blow clipped Jakyeong across the cheekbone, forcing him back a step. Jakyeong turned his head, spitting a dark mouthful of bloody saliva onto the hardwood.

Seeing the crimson on the floor, Il-hyun’s face instantly softened with guilt. "Sorry... I didn't mean to hit you that hard."

"Shut the fuck up!"

They collided again in a flurry of parries, sweeps, and takedowns. Nightstands were overturned, luxury decor flew through the air, and lamps shattered against the floor. A stray impact fractured the high-definition TV screen across the room, followed by a massive framed canvas crashing down from the wall, bursting into splinters.

Grappling across the rug, Jakyeong finally gained the upper hand, pinning Il-hyun to the floor and grabbing a fistful of his collar with a feral snarl:

"Say it! Swear you will never pull this shit again!"

Lying flat on his back, Il-hyun let out a breathy chuckle, his tongue lightly licking across his bruised lip.

"Ha... I love this position. Grind your hips against me just like that."

Beneath his thighs, Jakyeong felt the thick length of Il-hyun's cock swelling and hardening against his rear.

A wave of suffocating disgust and fury washed over him. How can someone get hard in the middle of a fistfight? The man isn't even human.

Jakyeong wound up, putting his entire weight into a punitive right hook. This time, Il-hyun didn't even raise a hand to block.

Crack.

The punch landed flush against Il-hyun's jaw just as the bedroom door clicked open.

Jakyeong snapped his head up to find Park Tae-soo frozen in the doorway, staring in absolute, stunned bewilderment.

Gathered around the breakfast table at dawn, Wang Han and Wang Ryun stared in wide-eyed shock as Jakyeong descended the staircase.

Seeing their notoriously heavy-sleeping youngest awake at the crack of dawn was surprising enough, but the split, purple bruise blooming across his lower lip drew an immediate gasp.

The senior housekeeper hurried over, her brow knit with concern. "Oh dear... Are you injured, Young Master?"

"I'm fine," Jakyeong muttered through clenched teeth.

Heavy, measured footsteps echoed from the upper hallway. It was Kang Il-hyun.

Jakyeong grabbed a fresh pastry from the bread basket, intending to retreat to his room, but Il-hyun had already rounded the landing. The moment he stepped into the dining room, Han and Ryun’s jaws dropped in unison.

A deep purple bruise colored Il-hyun’s cheekbone, paired with a crust of dried blood along his split lip.

The brothers shifted their stares back and forth between the two men. Last night, heavy, rhythmic thuds had rattled through the adjoining wall for nearly an hour, prompting Ryun to make crude jokes about the intensity of their bedroom antics.

They weren't fucking all night—they were beating the living hell out of each other.

"Good morning," Il-hyun greeted smoothly, flashing a bright, charming smile before fixing his gaze on Jakyeong.

He’d lost his temper and thrown a counter-punch during the brawl, but seeing the boy's tender, swollen lip stirred an uncomfortable twinge of guilt in his chest. As he moved closer to check the injury, Jakyeong snatched another roll and stormed up the stairs without sparing him a single glance.

Il-hyun’s eyes narrowed into slits. Why is he this furious?

He hurried up the steps after him, calling his name, but Jakyeong ignored the voice entirely. The boy darted down the corridor and slammed his bedroom door with a deafening BAM!

Il-hyun reached for the handle, only to freeze at the sound of deliberate footsteps approaching behind him.

He turned to find Wang Han standing at the top of the landing. Clearing his throat with a heavy ahem, Han scratched the bridge of his nose, stepping forward into the awkward silence.

Il-hyun greeted him with a polite, mask-like smile. "Did you need something, Mr. Wang?"

"President Kang... leave Wei—I mean, Jakyeong—alone."

Il-hyun arched a dark brow. The command rubbed him the wrong way. Sensing the prickle of hostility, Han chose his words with delicate, tactical care.

"He isolates himself completely for several days before executing a major assignment. He gets hyper-sensitive. If you keep provoking him like this, it will compromise the mission."

"Are you suggesting that I am provoking Lee Ja-kyeong?"

"Yes."

"Should I take that as a compliment?"

"No. What I mean is... Jakyeong despises that kind of behavior."

"What kind of behavior?"

Han hesitated, turning the phrasing over in his mind before delivering the verdict:

"Being clingy and suffocating."

Il-hyun’s expression hardened. Clingy? Me? The implication that he had been pestering the boy like some desperate suitor stung his pride.

"When he first came into our care at ten years old, Wang Ryun behaved just like you," Han explained calmly. "Ryun thought he was showing brotherly affection, but Jakyeong hated having someone constantly hovering in his personal space. They fought like mortal enemies for years. Though in truth, they still bicker like cats and dogs."

Il-hyun remained silent, taking in every word.

"This might sound overstepping coming from a contractor, President Kang... but if you continue smothering him, you will only breed deeper resentment."

Watching Il-hyun’s face, Han was privately stunned to see genuine, contemplative shock etched into the man's features. He had braced for an arrogant dismissal, yet the corporate boss seemed to be turning the critique over with dead-serious gravity. Is he actually sincere about this?

After a long pause, Il-hyun gave a slow, deliberate nod. "I shall take your counsel to heart. Thank you."

Hearing the uncharacteristic concession, Han let out an inward sigh of relief. Dealing with a ruthless, unpredictable client was always walking a razor's edge; having the man yield so graciously was a welcome miracle.

Once Il-hyun retreated downstairs, Han knocked lightly and slipped into Jakyeong’s suite.

Inside, two maintenance workers were busy clearing away the wreckage. Seeing the shattered table, cracked television, and fractured picture frames being hauled out in cardboard boxes, Han marveled at how intense the brawl must have been.

Jakyeong sat on the edge of the sectional, chewing mechanically on his dry roll, wincing whenever the bread brushed against the cut inside his mouth.

"You holding up?" Han asked, settling beside him.

Jakyeong gave a curt nod.

Looking around the ruined room, Han realized that keeping Jakyeong under the same roof as Kang Il-hyun would lead to daily bloodbaths. He quietly asked if Jakyeong would prefer moving the team to a separate, detached safehouse for the duration of the contract.

Jakyeong considered the proposal for a beat, then nodded firmly.

"Alright. I'll find the right moment to float the idea to President Kang."

Han gave Jakyeong’s shoulder two comforting pats. Jakyeong exhaled a long, heavy breath, tearing his pastry in half and handing the larger portion to Han. Even as a starving child on the streets of Macau, he had always split whatever food he scavenged right down the middle.

While Han chewed the bread, a cleaner hauled a large plastic crate out from the entertainment console.

Jakyeong casually glanced over, only for his eyes to lock onto a minuscule, pinhole lens embedded within the shattered casing of a digital clock. His brow pinched in immediate suspicion.

I wondered how that bastard always timed his intrusions so perfectly.

The entire suite was wired with covert surveillance cameras. A horrifying thought struck him: Did that psychotic freak record us in bed, too?

Knowing Il-hyun's paranoid, obsessive archival habits, the possibility was sickeningly high.

Gazing out through the tinted glass of his moving sedan, Kang Il-hyun wore a grim, deeply troubled frown.

In the front passenger seat, Park Tae-soo covertly tracked his master's expression through the rearview mirror. Wang Han’s lecture had struck Il-hyun like a physical blow.

Clingy? Suffocating? Me? To Lee Ja-kyeong?

He had genuinely believed he was treating the boy with unprecedented warmth and indulgence.

He had severed Choi Ki-tae's head and presented it on a silver platter; he had deployed an elite microsurgical team to reattach Wang Ryun’s severed finger without leaving a scar. How much more attentive could a man possibly be?

Should I have asked him for a hit list of everyone who ever crossed him and butchered them all? Would that finally get him to open his heart?

Il-hyun let out a quiet, frustrated sigh, shaking his head. To think that in the middle of a high-stakes corporate power struggle, he was sitting in the back of a car obsessing over relationship dynamics like an insecure schoolboy. The absurdity of it was pathetic.

"Shall we make a detour to the medical clinic, sir?" Tae-soo asked, noting the dark discoloration along Il-hyun's jawline.

Il-hyun touched the tender skin of his cheekbone. For someone with such delicate, boyish features, Jakyeong threw devastatingly fast, heavy hands. His footwork and counter-striking were so polished that matching him against a seasoned mercenary like Tae-soo in a no-holds-barred brawl would likely end in a dead draw.

Inevitably, his thoughts drifted right back to the boy.

"I've completely lost my mind," Il-hyun muttered aloud.

"Sir?" Tae-soo asked, glancing back.

Il-hyun waved a dismissive hand, leaning his head back against the headrest.

Closing his eyes, the memory of Jakyeong’s face from the other night flooded his senses—those dark, tear-rimmed eyes flushed with raw pleasure, the smooth, sun-baked skin beneath his palms, the intoxicating scent of his collarbone, and the breathless moans tangled with vicious curses.

Yet this morning, the kid had been genuinely, murderously furious. Tae-soo had reported that while the Wang brothers were ready to finalize the paperwork, Jakyeong was the sole holdout refusing to sign the retainer.

Does he truly despise me that much?

If I had just taxidermied him on the spot when I caught him in the rain... I wouldn't have to deal with this headache.

A bitter, self-deprecating smirk touched his lips.

Fuck.

I'm completely, hopelessly wrapped around his little finger.

Regretting that he hadn't stuffed and mounted the little stray when he had the chance, Il-hyun winced as the dull throb along his bruised jaw flared to life.
